# Static Analysis & Security Scanning Effectiveness

This dimension covers how well existing SAST/DAST/SCA tools detect vulnerabilities in AI-generated code and where the gaps are.

## The "97.8% Invisible" Finding

The most significant finding across all dimensions: traditional SAST tools miss nearly all formally-proven vulnerabilities in AI-generated code [2].

| Tool | Detection Rate | Notes |
|------|---------------|-------|
| COBALT Z3 SAT (formal verification) | 36.0% (90/250) | Formally proven exploitable |
| Semgrep (all rulesets) | 6.4% (16/250) | Pattern-based |
| Bandit (medium+) | 2.0% (5/250) | Python-focused |
| Combined Pattern Tools | 7.6% (19/250) | Semgrep + Bandit |
| Cppcheck 2.13 | 0.0% (0/87 C) | Heavyweight C analyzer |
| Clang Static Analyzer | 0.0% (0/87 C) | Heavyweight C analyzer |
| FlawFinder 2.0 | 4.6% (4/87 C) | Only strcat + rand |
| CodeQL v2.25.1 | **0.0% (0/90 Z3-proven)** | 100% miss across C and Python |

Tools missed **97.8% (88/90)** of formally Z3-proven vulnerabilities [2]. The 2.2% detected came from Semgrep/Bandit pattern matching, not heavyweight analyzers.

**Interpretation:** AI-generated code produces vulnerability patterns that existing SAST rules were not designed to detect. CodeQL found 4,241 CWEs in [1]'s GitHub analysis, but those are the *detectable* class — the formal verification in [2] reveals a much larger invisible class.

## CodeQL: Effective for Known Patterns, Blind to Novel Ones

- [1] found 4,241 CWE instances across 7,703 files using CodeQL — demonstrating CodeQL detects known vulnerability patterns
- [2] found CodeQL detected 0 of 90 Z3-proven vulnerabilities — demonstrating CodeQL misses the deeper semantic issues AI-generated code introduces
- These findings are complementary, not contradictory: CodeQL catches what its rules cover, but AI code introduces patterns outside those rules

## Generation-Review Asymmetry

Models can detect their own vulnerabilities better than they avoid creating them [2]:
- Self-detection rate: 78.7% (70/89 artifacts) when reviewing own code
- Generation vulnerability rate: 55.8% (mean)
- Per-model false-negative rates: 0% to 33%

This suggests adding an LLM-based review pass to CI/CD pipelines could catch vulnerabilities that SAST misses, though false-negative rates of up to 33% mean it cannot be the sole gate.

## AI-Enhanced Security Tools

**Google DeepMind CodeMender** [8]:
- 72 security fixes upstreamed to open-source in 6 months
- Projects up to 4.5M LOC
- Uses static analysis, dynamic analysis, differential testing, fuzzing, SMT solvers
- All patches human-reviewed before submission
- Would have "rendered unexploitable" CVE-2023-4863 (libwebp)

CodeMender's multi-technique approach (including SMT solvers) parallels the COBALT Z3 SAT methodology from [2] and addresses exactly the gap that traditional tools miss.

## Security Mitigation via Fine-Tuning

From [3] (SLR):
- SVEN_sec (security-hardened fine-tuning): achieved >85% security (up to 92.3% for 2.7B parameter model)
- SVEN_vul (degraded): reduced security by 22.3–25.3%

This demonstrates specialized fine-tuning can substantially improve code security, but it requires model-level intervention — not just prompt engineering.

## Auto-Repair Limitations

From [3]:
- C code repair: only 2.2% auto-fixable
- SQL injection repair: only 29.6% of 10,796 programs repairable
- Java vulnerability repair: only 20.4% fixable

From [5] (search snippets): 55.5% of Copilot vulnerabilities fixable with AI chat assistance.

## RCI (Recursive Criticism and Improvement)

The OpenSSF guide [20] recommends the RCI technique: asking AI to "review your previous answer and find problems" then "improve your answer." Claims to reduce security weaknesses "by an order of magnitude with 2 iterations." The original study for this claim was not traced in this session.

## Gaps and Limitations

- Only open-source/free SAST tools tested in [2] — Snyk, Checkmarx, Fortify not evaluated
- The 97.8% finding was on C and Python only; JavaScript, Java, TypeScript untested
- No study compares DAST or IAST effectiveness on AI-generated code
- SCA effectiveness for detecting AI-hallucinated packages is not quantified in any source
- Commercial SAST tools with AI-enhanced capabilities (Snyk DeepCode, SonarQube AI) were not independently benchmarked
